title_en: Wuhan Gas Company v. Chongqing Instrumentation Factory — dispute over gas meter assembly line technology transfer contract and gas meter parts purchase and sale contract

full_text_en:
Wuhan Gas Company v. Chongqing Detection Instrument Factory — dispute over gas meter assembly line technology transfer contract and gas meter parts purchase and sale contract

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Wuhan Gas Company.

Legal Representative: Chen Ziman, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Xuefeng, Deputy Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Wenlai, Lawyer of Wuhan Law Firm.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Chongqing Detection Instrument Factory.

Legal Representative: Zhang Benyan, Factory Director of the Factory.

Agent ad litem: Liu Hong, Staff Member of the Factory.

Agent ad litem: Ke Ruiqing, Lawyer of Chongqing No.3 Law Firm.

The plaintiff Wuhan Gas Company (hereinafter referred to as the Gas Company) filed a lawsuit with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province against the defendant Chongqing Detection Instrument Factory (hereinafter referred to as the Instrument Factory) concerning a dispute over a gas meter assembly line technology transfer contract and a gas meter parts purchase and sale contract.

The plaintiff Gas Company alleged: The plaintiff and the defendant respectively signed the "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the J2.5 Gas Meter Assembly Line" and the "Supply Contract for J2.5 Gas Meter Parts" and supplementary agreements in September 1987. After the agreements were signed, the defendant failed to fully perform the technology transfer contract, did not provide the plaintiff with the drawings and molds, fixtures, etc. for the J2.5 gas meter reverse meter, did not assist the plaintiff in assembling 500 qualified reverse meters, and did not supply the plaintiff with a sufficient quantity of J2.5 gas meter parts and accessories, resulting in the J2.5 gas meter production line being unable to be put into use. At the same time, the defendant did not supply the plaintiff with sufficient parts in accordance with the provisions of the gas meter parts supply contract. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order: 1. Return the J2.5 gas meter assembly line transferred by the defendant to the plaintiff, and compensate the plaintiff for the investment losses in the J2.5 gas meter assembly line project; 2. The plaintiff to pay liquidated damages for non-delivery of RMB 1,031,400, and bear liquidated damages for delayed delivery of RMB 257,850.

The defendant Instrument Factory argued: The assembly line technology transfer contract signed by both parties had been basically performed. The plaintiff's claim for return of the assembly line and compensation for investment losses was untenable. The defendant's failure to fully perform the gas meter parts supply contract was due to an objective change of circumstances that could not be foreseen or prevented, which made the defendant lose the ability to continue performing the contract. The defendant had no subjective fault regarding this change of circumstances, and therefore should not bear liability for breach of contract. The defendant had repeatedly negotiated with the plaintiff to modify the contract, but the plaintiff did not cooperate, leading to the dispute. At the same time, a counterclaim was filed: requesting the plaintiff to bear liquidated damages for overdue payment of technical documentation fees and equipment fees amounting to RMB 117,501.28.

The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court found through trial: In September 1987, the plaintiff Gas Company and the defendant Instrument Factory signed a "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the J2.5 Gas Meter Assembly Line" and a supplementary agreement in Wuhan, stipulating: The Instrument Factory would transfer the J2.5 gas meter assembly technology to the Gas Company, provide all molds, fixtures, special equipment, and complete sets of technical drawings and documents for the assembly line, establish a J2.5 gas meter assembly line with an annual production capacity of 50,000 units for the Gas Company, and technically guide the Gas Company to assemble 1,000 qualified forward meters and 500 reverse meters; the Instrument Factory should give priority to meeting the production needs of the Gas Company's assembly line, provide a sufficient quantity of J2.5 gas meter parts and accessories (excluding raw and auxiliary materials), ensure the quality of the parts, and be responsible for training 10–15 assembly, maintenance, and inspection personnel for the Gas Company. The Gas Company should pay the Instrument Factory RMB 500,000 for all drawings and documentation fees, RMB 200,000 for molds, fixtures, special equipment, and inspection equipment fees (excluding freight), and RMB 100,000 for technical cooperation fees, totaling RMB 800,000. Within 2 months after the contract took effect, the Gas Company would pay the Instrument Factory 90% of the technical documentation fee, i.e., RMB 450,000. Within 10 days after receipt of the payment, the Instrument Factory would provide all documentation to the Gas Company. After trial production and the Gas Company's verification that all documentation was complete, the remaining 10% balance would be paid. The term of the contract was 3 years. On October 29 of the same year, the parties further signed a "Meeting Minutes" making additional provisions on matters not covered in the assembly contract, and thereafter the parties began to perform the contract. From November 1987 to June 1988, the Instrument Factory successively delivered drawings and technical documentation to the Gas Company and provided molds, fixtures, and related spare parts; the Gas Company successively paid 90% of the drawing and documentation fees, i.e., RMB 450,000, and 70% of the mold, fixture, and equipment fees, i.e., RMB 140,000. In April 1988, after the Gas Company paid the technical cooperation fee of RMB 100,000, the Instrument Factory provided technical training in Chongqing to 22 personnel selected by the Gas Company. In June of the same year, the parties conducted acceptance and signed four acceptance agreements and reports concerning the J2.5 gas meter assembly line technology transfer contract. Immediately thereafter, the Gas Company paid the Instrument Factory the remaining 10% balance of the drawing and documentation fees, i.e., RMB 50,000, and RMB 50,000 of the remaining 30% balance of the mold, fixture, etc. fees (with a remaining balance of RMB 10,000 to be paid in a lump sum after the contract term expired). At this point, the Gas Company had paid the Instrument Factory RMB 790,000 of the total technology transfer fee of RMB 800,000. The forward meter technology transfer specified in the "Technology Transfer Cooperation Contract" and its supplementary agreements was basically completed, but the reverse meter technology transfer was not fulfilled. On May 6, 1989, the Gas Company sent a letter to the Instrument Factory requesting full performance of the contract and supplementary agreements. The Instrument Factory believed that it had performed the contract as agreed and that the reverse meter technology was not part of its contractual obligations.

At the same time as signing the aforementioned technology transfer contract and its supplementary agreements, the parties also signed a "Supply Contract for J2.5 Gas Meter Parts" and a supplementary agreement, stipulating: The Instrument Factory would supply the Gas Company with 70,000 sets of domestically produced J2.5 gas meter parts. Among them, 30,000 sets would be supplied in 1988 (60% forward meter parts, to be supplied monthly on average starting from April 25 of that year; 40% reverse meter parts, to be supplied monthly on average starting from September 25 of that year); 40,000 sets would be supplied in 1989 (40% reverse meter parts), to be supplied monthly on average, with a unit price of RMB 57.3 per set (including packaging costs), totaling RMB 4,011,000. Payment would be made by bank collection and acceptance within 10 days after the goods arrived and were accepted by the Gas Company. The contract also stipulated product quality, transportation methods, product packaging, and liability for breach of contract. Thereafter, in three shipments on May 6, June 23, and August 19, 1988, the Instrument Factory delivered 10,000 sets of forward meter parts to the Gas Company. After the Gas Company actually accepted and paid for the goods and freight totaling RMB 525,364.35, it refused to pay RMB 50,287.14 on the grounds of insufficient quantity and substandard quality, and also owed the Instrument Factory RMB 3,597.84 for material purchases. On November 23 of the same year, the Gas Company sent a letter to the Instrument Factory requesting performance of the parts supply contract. On December 20 of the same year, the Instrument Factory replied to the Gas Company, requesting an increase in the price of the parts due to rapid market changes and rising prices. On March 25, 1989, the Instrument Factory sent a "Letter Regarding Further Negotiation on the Price of J2.5 Gas Meter Parts" to the Gas Company, proposing that, given that the cost of parts had risen to RMB 79.22 per set and the price verified by the price control department was RMB 83 per set, it was willing to forego profit and bear certain economic losses as much as possible, offering a final price of RMB 75.50 per set for modifying or terminating the gas meter parts supply contract signed by the parties. The Gas Company still required the Instrument Factory to perform at the original contract price. The Instrument Factory then stopped supplying gas meter parts to the Gas Company, leading to a dispute between the parties.

The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court held: The "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the Gas Meter Assembly Line" and the supplementary agreement, as well as the "Supply Contract for Gas Meter Parts" and the supplementary agreement, entered into by the plaintiff Gas Company and the defendant Instrument Factory, were established on the basis of equality, mutual benefit, equivalent compensation, and consensus. Their contents did not violate the relevant provisions of national policies. The contracts were valid and should be protected by law. In performing the "Supply Contract for Gas Meter Parts" and the supplementary agreement, the Instrument Factory, by citing price changes during economic reform and demanding price modification, refused to perform its contractual obligations, leading to the dispute. In accordance with Article 34 of the "Regulations on Purchase and Sale Contracts for Industrial and Mineral Products," it should bear full responsibility. In performing the "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the Gas Meter Assembly Line" and the supplementary agreement, the Instrument Factory's failure to provide the Gas Company with reverse meter technology as stipulated in the contract constituted a breach of contract. In accordance with Article 32, Paragraph 1, and Article 35 of the "Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," it should also bear full responsibility. The actual expenses incurred by the Instrument Factory in training the Gas Company's personnel should be borne by the Gas Company. The parts supplied by the Instrument Factory to the Gas Company were produced using proprietary technology introduced by the Instrument Factory; these parts had to be assembled using the assembly line and technology supplied by the Instrument Factory and were specialized products. The assembly line could only generate benefits by relying on the parts supplied by the Instrument Factory. The Instrument Factory's refusal to supply parts to the Gas Company eliminated the material basis for the continued existence of the assembly line, and the assembly line should be returned. Accordingly, the court ruled: 1. The unperformed portions of the "Supply Contract for J2.5 Gas Meter Parts" and the supplementary agreement signed by both parties were terminated; 2. The Instrument Factory shall pay the Gas Company liquidated damages for the undelivered portion amounting to RMB 688,231.89; 3. The Gas Company shall return to the Instrument Factory substandard parts valued at RMB 47,868.28, and the Instrument Factory shall bear the loss of raw and auxiliary materials for dismantling the substandard parts amounting to RMB 1,847.74, and the freight loss caused by the wrong consignment station amounting to RMB 571.12 (which the Gas Company had already refused to pay); 4. The Gas Company shall pay the Instrument Factory RMB 3,597.84 for material purchases; 5. The "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the J2.5 Gas Meter Assembly Line" and the supplementary agreement signed by both parties were rescinded; 6. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the Instrument Factory shall go to the Gas Company to collect all the technical documentation it had supplied, dismantle the J2.5 gas meter assembly line at its own expense, and the Gas Company shall provide the necessary working conditions for dismantling the assembly line. If the Instrument Factory fails to do so within the time limit, the Gas Company shall not be responsible, and the Instrument Factory shall pay the actual storage costs of the assembly line; 7. The Instrument Factory shall refund to the Gas Company RMB 500,000 for drawing and documentation fees, RMB 190,000 for mold, fixture, special equipment, and testing equipment fees, and RMB 50,000 for part of the technical cooperation fees, totaling RMB 740,000; 8. The Instrument Factory shall compensate the Gas Company for losses on the J2.5 gas meter assembly line amounting to RMB 184,478. The total of items 2, 4, 7, and 8 amounted to RMB 1,609,112.05 payable by the Instrument Factory to the Gas Company, to be paid in full within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment.

The defendant Instrument Factory, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Hubei Provincial High People's Court, arguing: The judgment of first instance had unclear findings of fact and improper application of law; there was no legal basis for rescinding the assembly line technology transfer contract; although the gas meter assembly line technology transfer contract and the parts supply contract were related, this should not lead to the rescission of the assembly line technology transfer contract; requiring the appellant Instrument Factory to compensate the Gas Company for losses on the assembly line lacked factual basis and reasoning; the technology transfer contract had been fully performed, and the technology transfer fee should not be refunded. The failure to continue performing the parts supply contract as agreed was due to a material change in objective circumstances, not subjective fault on the part of the appellant, so it should not bear liquidated damages; the judgment of first instance did not address the counterclaim filed by the appellant. The appellant requested the court of second instance to quash the original judgment and render a fair ruling in accordance with the law.

The appellee Gas Company believed that the judgment of first instance was correct and requested the court of second instance to uphold it.

The Hubei Provincial High People's Court held: This case consisted of two independent contracts. The "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the J2.5 Gas Meter Assembly Line" and its supplementary agreement signed by the appellee Gas Company and the appellant Instrument Factory were legally valid and should be protected by law. In performing this contract, the Instrument Factory neither assisted the Gas Company in assembling 500 qualified reverse meters nor imparted the practical operating techniques for assembling reverse meters to the Gas Company's technical personnel, which constituted a breach of contract. However, in the judgment of first instance, while it confirmed the validity of the assembly line technology transfer contract on the one hand, and dealt with the valid contract as if it were an invalid contract by ordering the Instrument Factory to return the technology transfer fees and the Gas Company to return the assembly line (to be dismantled by the Instrument Factory) and all technical documentation on the other hand, this was inconsistent with the law, especially given that the technology transfer contract signed by the parties had been substantially performed, the Gas Company had sent personnel to receive technical training, mastered the drawings, documentation, and forward meter assembly technology, and the gas meter production line had been put into operation and generated economic benefits. Regarding the gas meter parts supply contract, during the performance of the contract, an unforeseeable and unpreventable change of circumstances occurred: the state-set price of aluminum ingots, the main raw material for producing gas meter parts, had increased from RMB 4,400 to 4,600 per ton at the time of signing the contract to RMB 16,000 per ton, and the selling price of the aluminum shell correspondingly increased from RMB 23.085 per set to RMB 41 per set. If the Instrument Factory were still required to supply gas meter parts at the original contract price, it would be manifestly unfair. For the dispute arising from this, the principle of fairness and good faith as stipulated in Article 4 of the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China" and the provisions of Article 27, Paragraph 1, Item 4 of the Economic Contract Law should be applied, and the principle of change of circumstances should be applied to handle the matter fairly and reasonably. The judgment of first instance, by applying the relevant provisions on liability for breach of contract in the Economic Contract Law and the "Regulations on Purchase and Sale Contracts for Industrial and Mineral Products," ordering the Instrument Factory to bear liability for breach of contract, was clearly inappropriate. Furthermore, the Instrument Factory had clearly raised a counterclaim in the first instance, but the judgment of first instance did not explain whether the counterclaim was established or whether it could be consolidated with the main action. Accordingly, the Hubei Provincial High People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (3) and (4) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," ruled: Quash the judgment of first instance and remand the case to the original trial court for retrial.

The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court lawfully reconstituted a collegial panel and consolidated the main action and counterclaim for retrial. Under the mediation conducted by the court, the parties voluntarily reached the following mediation agreement: 1. The "Cooperation Contract on Technology Transfer of the J2.5 Gas Meter Assembly Line" and the "Supply Contract for J2.5 Gas Meter Parts" are terminated; 2. The Gas Company shall return parts valued at RMB 48,070.30 to the Instrument Factory, and the Instrument Factory shall bear the loss of RMB 3,597.84 used for purchasing materials; 3. The Instrument Factory shall pay the Gas Company a lump sum compensation of RMB 210,000, to be paid within 30 days after the mediation document takes effect.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance of this case, RMB 12,774, shall be borne by the Gas Company; the court acceptance fee for the second instance, RMB 38,460, shall be borne by the Instrument Factory.
